question: Policy #1833 serialises root-core because its git-range mover specs go red under parallel scheduling. The mission's premise was that the other four suites carry no such constraint and pay ~30 minutes per capture for another suite's flake. Each was measured rather than assumed.

findings.reason: packages/mcp-server/vitest.config.ts sets fileParallelism:false in its own config, because its pack specs run prepack builds that replace shared workspace dist trees. Forced parallel: 120 failed suites and only 6,801 of the serial 7,263 tests collected at all.
policy #1833, unchanged and not re-litigated here.

findings.verdict: stays serial, on the arithmetic rather than a hard constraint
findings.reason: Six parallel runs, three serial. Parallel run 1, taken at the highest load observed in the session, failed chart-titles.s201's label-overlap assertion — it reads the settled positions of an ECharts force-directed layout, which is iterative and therefore timing-dependent. Runs 2-6 and all three serial runs matched the baseline exactly. The suite is 28s of a 2,472s capture, so parallelism buys seconds while admitting a timing-sensitive geometry assertion into the receipt.

findings.verdict: parallel is clean, and worth nothing
findings.reason: Three back-to-back parallel runs matched the serial baseline exactly at 72/72/0. The suite is 11s.

findings.verdict: parallel is clean, and worth about twenty seconds
findings.reason: Three back-to-back runs at package defaults matched the serial baseline exactly at 1,485/1,485/0. The suite is 52s serial.

conclusion: There is almost nothing to win by un-serialising. mcp-server and root-core are 2,381s of the 2,472s certified capture — 96% — and both are serial for stated, measured reasons. The three fast suites together are 91s, 3.7%. The capture's real costs are elsewhere, and s204-m01 took them there: the per-call ledger read (census-cost/), the 170s single-test outlier moved to an on-demand gate, and the ninety-second tripwire that stops a thirty-four-minute discovery.

decision.note: Scheduling is now decided PER SUITE with its reason recorded on the receipt, instead of one blanket --serial applied to all five because of root-core. That is the part worth keeping: the blanket flag is exactly what CMOS learning #655 objected to, and it hid which constraint belonged to which suite.

serial.mcp-server: its own vitest.config.ts fileParallelism:false — pack prepack builds replace shared dist trees
serial.viz-core: s204-m01: one parallel failure in a force-layout geometry assertion; 28s suite, so the saving does not pay for the flake

decision.measuredSaving: roughly 35 seconds of a 2,472-second capture. Scheduling was not the cost.
